title: Does Waxing Get Easier the More You Do It?
summary: Does waxing hurt less over time? Learn what to expect from your first wax to six months of consistent waxing, including pain levels and regrowth changes.
body_markdown:
If your first wax had you questioning if you'd willingly do that again, read this before you throw in the towel.


It's true that your first wax is usually the hardest—that’s not a myth. But there are reasons for that, and plenty of ways to make the experience more comfortable. We'll break down why your first wax can hurt more, what to expect from your second and third appointments, and how regular waxing can make a difference over time.


Spoiler: the best is yet to come.


## Does Waxing Hurt Less the More You Do It?


Yes, waxing generally becomes easier and less painful the more consistently you do it. With regular waxing, hair can grow back finer, softer, and less dense, making it easier to remove from the root. That also means less painful waxing and more manageable regrowth over time.


There's a mental side to it as well. Once you know what to expect, you're less likely to tense up in anticipation of discomfort. Feeling relaxed is an underrated way to make your waxing experience feel easier.


While waxing will never be completely painless, most guests find that their appointments become noticeably more comfortable as they maintain a consistent routine.


## What to Expect When You Keep Waxing


The benefits of regular waxing don't happen overnight, but you may start noticing a difference sooner than you think. Here's a glimpse at how your hair growth, comfort, and results can change from your first appointment through six months of consistent waxing.


**Wax Appointment**


**What to Expect**


First Wax


Thicker, more deeply rooted hair. Typically the most uncomfortable.


Second Wax


Less hair to remove, less anticipation of discomfort.


Third Wax


More even regrowth, easier hair removal, a more comfortable experience.


After Six Months


Hair may grow back finer and sparser, with less noticeable regrowth between appointments.


## Your First Wax: Why It's Usually the Hardest


Your first wax is typically the most uncomfortable, and there are a few reasons for this.


-


Thicker, more deeply rooted hair:


Your hair is at its thickest, with strong roots that make removal more uncomfortable.


-


Different stages of hair growth:


Hair grows in cycles, so your first wax removes hairs at different stages, including thicker, more stubborn ones.


-


Anticipation of pain:


Not knowing what to expect can make you tense up, which can make the discomfort feel more intense. To help prepare yourself, read more about


[what a wax feels like](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/experts-answers-does-waxing-hurt) .


### How to make your first wax hurt less.


There is good news. If you're worried about discomfort, choosing an experienced Wax Specialist for your first time can make a real difference.


[Our Wax Specialists](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/our-wax-specialists-are-your-wax-specialists) are specially trained in techniques that help minimize discomfort, and our exclusive


[Comfort Wax®](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/how-our-comfort-wax-redefined-the-waxing-experience) is designed to grip hair without pulling at your skin. There are a number of


[ways to make your first wax more comfortable,](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/how-to-make-waxing-more-comfortable-a-guide-to-a-more-comfortable-wax) but choosing an experienced professional is the most important one.


It's also okay to be nervous! We've helped countless guests through their first wax. Let your Wax Specialist know it's your first time. They can explain each step, answer your questions, and help you feel more comfortable throughout your appointment.


For more tips, check out


[What to Expect During Your First Wax](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/what-to-expect-during-your-first-wax) .


## Your Second Wax: It Starts Getting Easier


By your second wax, you may already notice that the experience feels more manageable. Hair grows in cycles, and after your first wax, not every hair grows back at the same time. That means there may be fewer hairs to remove during your second appointment, which can help reduce discomfort.


It also helps that you know what to expect this time around, so you're less likely to tense up in anticipation. Sometimes, simply feeling more relaxed makes all the difference.


## Your Third Wax: Smoother, More Even Results


By your third wax, your consistency is starting to pay off. With regular appointments, more of your hair may begin growing on a similar schedule, making it easier to achieve smoother, more even results.


You may also start noticing that hair releases more easily from the follicle. As you continue waxing, follicles can weaken, making regrowth more manageable. This contributes to making your overall experience feel more comfortable than your first appointment.


****


## After Six Months of Consistent Waxing: Less Hair, Less Upkeep


Keep waxing once a month for six months, and you may start to notice real changes in your hair growth and the results of your waxes.


-


Finer, softer, and sparser regrowth:


Hair may become less coarse and dense over time. (The idea that waxing makes hair grow back thicker? Yeah,


[that’s a myth](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/3-debunked-myths-about-waxing) .)


-


Smoother, more consistent results:


Regular waxing can help keep hair growth cycles more closely aligned.


-


Less noticeable hair between appointments:


You may find that regrowth becomes easier to manage, making


[wax results last longer.](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/what-to-know-about-how-long-does-waxing-last)


-


Easier, more comfortable hair removal:


Finer regrowth may make hairs easier to remove.


Results vary depending on genetics, hormones, and the area being waxed. Waxing isn't permanent hair removal, but consistency can make a noticeable difference over time.


## Make the Most of Your Results With Aftercare


Consistency isn't the only way to make your waxes last longer. The right aftercare can help, too. Our


[EWC SLOW® collection](https://waxcenter.com/collections/all) features


[narcissus bulb extract](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/the-secret-to-slowing-hair-regrowth) to help reduce the appearance of hair thickness, so regrowth looks finer between appointments.


For more aftercare, check out the


[3 Steps of Your In-Between Wax Routine](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/the-3-steps-of-your-in-between-wax-routine) .


## Does Taking a Long Break From Waxing Reset Your Progress?


Taking a long break from waxing can affect your progress and make your next appointment feel more uncomfortable. After a gap of six to eight weeks or more, hair may grow back at different stages and become longer and more noticeable between appointments.


This is why committing to a monthly wax is better than waxing occasionally. You’ll keep building on your results and ultimately get better value out of your services. The more consistent you are with your routine, the more you can expect smooth results, more manageable regrowth, and more comfortable appointments.


For smoother results and a more comfortable experience, we generally recommend waxing[every three to four weeks](https://waxcenter.com/blogs/news/how-often-should-you-wax-each-body-area-a-head-to-toe-schedule) .

The first wax might be the hardest, but it doesn't have to define your waxing experience. With each appointment, you become more familiar with the process, and over time, waxing becomes easier.


The real payoff? Less time thinking about unwanted hair and more time enjoying smooth skin.
